description: UCI row 45 (age 35, MEDIUM vulnerability, moderate knowledge, RT 3, horizon 2yr) — structured note: all hard rules pass (score 100) -> SUITABLE
client_narrative: Kristoffer Lund is 35 years old and works as an accountant at a logistics company. He earns approximately 31,900 euros per year and holds 2,500 euros in liquid savings. He wants to invest 1,800 euros for about 2 years to earn better returns than a savings account while limiting downside risk. His investment knowledge is moderate: he understands the basics of bonds and structured products and has previously held bank-issued structured notes. He rates his risk tolerance at 3 out of 10 — cautious but not entirely risk-averse — and has stated he cannot afford to lose his investment. His investment objective is asset growth.
product_narrative: The product is a capital-at-risk structured note that provides conditional coupon payments linked to the performance of a basket of European equity indices. Coupons are paid only if all index levels remain above a predefined barrier on specified observation dates; if any index closes below the barrier at maturity, the investor receives a reduced capital repayment proportional to the worst-performing index. The note is classified as a complex financial instrument under MiFID II, publishes a KID, and does not require any specific minimum knowledge level in its terms. It uses no leverage and has a minimum recommended holding period of two years. In barrier breach scenarios partial capital loss results.
